.. _const-vendor-pairing:

Const-Vendor Pairing
---------------------

**Every module under** :mod:`pcapkit.const` **is generated by a matching crawler
under** :mod:`pcapkit.vendor`. A registry copied from an IANA, IETF or similar
web-published table is never hand-maintained -- the crawler re-scrapes the source and
regenerates the module, so a hand edit to the generated file is silently discarded on
the next run. :issue:`2441`, raised in cross-review and knowingly deferred rather than
fixed.

The Exception
~~~~~~~~~~~~~

**A source that is not a web-crawlable table is the one legitimate reason to hand-write
a const module.** :class:`~pcapkit.const.linux.arphrd.ARPHRD`'s source is the Linux
kernel header ``<linux/if_arp.h>``, not an IANA page, and its docstring says so plainly
-- *"Only the values that pcapkit names are listed"* -- rather than claiming full
coverage from a registry :mod:`pcapkit.vendor` could crawl. The ``EnumRegistry`` shape
it was moved to on :pr:`2443` is a structural decision for API uniformity with every
other registry, not a claim that a crawler produces the file.

Known Violation
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

:class:`~pcapkit.const.tls.content_type.ContentType` and
:class:`~pcapkit.const.tls.handshake_type.HandshakeType` (:pr:`2441`) both cite a live
IANA registry and claim to name every value IANA assigns, with no
:mod:`pcapkit.vendor` crawler behind either one -- no ``pcapkit/vendor/tls/``
directory exists, and neither class appears in :data:`pcapkit.vendor.__all__`. This
was flagged in that PR's own review and merged anyway on the stated reasoning that the
crawler would follow later. Tracked as :issue:`2495`.
